look: XORA site look, same as the V00 welcome film: deep void ground, frosted glass panels with thin cyan-to-violet edges, fictional market lines drawing in, calm eased motion, the brain tutor guiding from the bottom-right corner

scenes.name: Lesson twenty-two
scenes.desc: Title card: Phase 5, lesson T22, Position Sizing and Risk Budget; a risk bar fills to a budget line; the tutor walks in.

scenes.name: Same stop, different damage
scenes.desc: Two traders buy fictional BTC at 60,000 with a stop at 59,400; notional 500 vs 10,000 USDT; price falls to the stop: -5 vs -100 USDT, account bars shrink.

scenes.name: Balance and risk budget
scenes.desc: Account balance and risk-per-trade budget defined; fair-spending analogy; a 1,000 USDT practice account with a 10 USDT example budget slice.

scenes.name: Stop distance
scenes.desc: Stop distance defined; long: 60,000 to 59,400 = 600 USDT = 1%; short: 60,000 to 60,300 = 300 USDT = 0.5%.

scenes.name: Size and notional
scenes.desc: Position size and notional defined; 0.01 BTC x 60,000 = 600 USDT; a 1% fall loses 6 USDT; rice-bag analogy.

scenes.name: Allowed notional
scenes.desc: Allowed notional = risk / (|entry - stop| / entry): 10 / 0.01 = 1,000 USDT (about 0.0167 BTC); short 10 / 0.005 = 2,000 USDT; a simple model.

scenes.name: Leverage exposure
scenes.desc: Leverage = notional / margin; 1,000 USDT notional needs 500 / 200 / 100 margin at 2x / 5x / 10x; loss at the stop stays about 10 USDT; liquidation risk.

scenes.name: Drawdown
scenes.desc: Drawdown defined; five 10 USDT losses: 1,000 to 950 (5%); five 100 USDT losses: 1,000 to 500 (50%), needing +100% to recover.

scenes.name: Leverage first
scenes.desc: Mistake: choosing leverage or size first; fix: budget, stop, notional, then margin; NO_TRADE when the size makes no sense.

scenes.name: Try it
scenes.desc: Account 2,000, example budget 20 USDT, long 50,000, stop 49,500; options 200 / 2,000 / 20,000 USDT; countdown; answer B with working, why not C.

scenes.name: Inputs that make no sense
scenes.desc: An educational mock calculator flags zero stop distance, a stop on the wrong side, and a budget bigger than the account.

scenes.name: Know the limits
scenes.desc: Slippage and fees; liquidation before the stop at high leverage; minimum sizes; fictional examples, no recommended percentages; NO_TRADE allowed.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Three key points and a check question: risk 10 USDT, stop 2% away, allowed notional 500 USDT.

scenes.name: Up next
scenes.desc: End card: next lesson T23, Full Scalping Decision Lifecycle.
